design: Tier 2 (a permission boundary). Operator approved the design in chat on 2026-10-07 (Approve (Recommended)). Hazard: none to data or the running Hub; no migration, nothing restarts. The behavioural risk is a real Codex binary treating the policy differently from the scripted session (a wrapped command text, or a read-only sandbox blocking aw-tool's network before it asks), which fails closed: the spec turn cannot reach the Hub through the call command, and the MCP form is unaffected. Rollback: revert the commit. Same rules as Copilot's spec turn (copilot_acp._decide_permission: the Hub's own call first, every other edit refused), stricter on commands because Codex has a real sandbox and an approval is a request to leave it. The shell dialect given to _hub_own_call follows the platform Codex runs on (PowerShell on Windows, Bash elsewhere).

problem: F4's rule, that a turn triggered with a specification document open loses file-write tools regardless of phase, rigor or posture, is applied as restrict_spec_writes=bool(spec_document) on the runner request. codex exec honours it with --sandbox read-only (runner_commands.py). app-server reads no argv, and CodexAppServerTransport.run_turn passes neither the flag nor anything derived from it, so the thread starts under the posture's own sandbox (workspace-write, or danger-full-access under Full access) and a Codex agent on a spec turn can write files. Found from code in each-runner-cli-is-one-adapter R2 (D11), confirmed by its Opus review, never driven.

requirements.rationale: The sandbox is Codex's real write barrier. never is excluded because under it Codex refuses the Hub's own arguments-file write silently instead of asking, and a turn told the call command could not submit the document it was opened on.
requirements.statement: A Codex app-server turn opened on a specification document MUST start its thread with sandbox read-only in every permission posture, with approval policy untrusted under Ask me and on-request otherwise.

requirements.rationale: An approval is the only way out of a read-only sandbox, so answering it by the posture would hand back what the sandbox took away. Under Ask me a command still goes to the operator, who answers it as today.
requirements.statement: On such a turn the system MUST decline every file-change approval, and every command-execution approval outside Ask me, that is not the Hub's own call, in every posture and without an operator card for a file change.

requirements.rationale: The one write a spec turn keeps (a-run-reaches-the-hub-without-mcp D16); it is bounded by the run's own credential.
requirements.statement: On such a turn the system MUST accept a file change whose every path is a .json file inside the calls root, and a command that is exactly one aw-tool invocation, as mcp_server._hub_own_call defines them, in every posture.

requirements.rationale: The restriction is the document's, not a narrowing of any posture.
requirements.statement: A turn with no specification document open, and the answer to an MCP elicitation on any turn, MUST behave as before.

Claude and Copilot spec turns, governed by their own adapters

summary: A turn opened on a specification document starts its Codex app-server thread read-only in every posture, declines every file change and sandbox escape that is not the Hub's own call, and keeps the Hub's own call (the arguments file and aw-tool) and its MCP tools. Today the restriction never reaches app-server, Codex's default transport (F462).
